description: The chemistry and cell biology a computing student needs before bioinformatics: proteins, enzymes, metabolism, membranes, the cell cycle and gene regulation. In the lab students fit enzyme kinetics, simulate pathways and signalling, and interpret the data that wet-lab techniques produce.
modelledOn: Nelson and Cox, Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry
Alberts et al., Molecular Biology of the Cell
outcomes: Describe the structure of amino acids and proteins and explain how sequence determines folding and function.
Fit Michaelis-Menten and inhibition models to enzyme data and interpret the kinetic parameters.
Trace carbon and energy through glycolysis, the citric acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation, and model a small pathway as a system of equations.
Explain membrane transport, cell signalling, the cell cycle and the origins of cancer in terms of molecular mechanisms.
Model gene regulation with simple dynamical and Boolean networks and interpret the output of common laboratory assays.

units.title: Chemistry of life
topics: Atoms, covalent and non-covalent bonds; water as solvent and hydrogen bonding
Acids, bases, pH and buffers; the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation
Functional groups and the four classes of biomolecule: carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids
Thermodynamics of reactions: free energy, enthalpy, entropy and equilibrium constants
Coupled reactions and the role of ATP as an energy currency

units.title: Amino acids, proteins and structure
topics: The 20 amino acids: side-chain classes, charge, pKa and isoelectric point
The peptide bond, backbone angles and the Ramachandran plot
Levels of structure: primary, secondary (alpha helix, beta sheet), tertiary and quaternary
Protein folding, the hydrophobic effect, chaperones and misfolding diseases
Haemoglobin and myoglobin: oxygen binding, cooperativity and sickle cell disease
Protein databases and formats: UniProt entries and PDB files as data

units.title: Enzymes and kinetics
topics: How enzymes lower activation energy; active sites, cofactors and specificity
Michaelis-Menten kinetics: derivation, Km, Vmax and kcat
Linearised plots versus non-linear least-squares curve fitting
Competitive, uncompetitive and non-competitive inhibition; drug action
Allosteric enzymes, the Hill equation and feedback regulation
Enzyme assays: progress curves, initial rates, replicates and error bars

units.title: Metabolism and energy flow
topics: Catabolism and anabolism; the major pathways as a network
Glycolysis: ten steps, regulation by phosphofructokinase, net ATP and NADH
Pyruvate oxidation and the citric acid cycle
Electron transport and oxidative phosphorylation; the proton gradient and ATP synthase
Gluconeogenesis, glycogen and fat metabolism; hormonal control by insulin and glucagon
Pathways as stoichiometric matrices; steady state and an introduction to flux balance

units.title: Membranes, transport and cell signalling
topics: Membrane structure: the fluid mosaic, lipid bilayers and membrane proteins
Passive diffusion, facilitated transport and active transport; the sodium-potassium pump
Membrane potential: the Nernst and Goldman equations; the action potential
Receptors, G proteins, kinase cascades and second messengers
Signalling as an information network: amplification, feedback and crosstalk

units.title: Cell structure, the cell cycle and cancer
topics: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells; organelles and the cytoskeleton
The cell cycle: phases, cyclins, CDKs and checkpoints
Mitosis and meiosis; chromosomes, crossing over and the origin of genetic variation
Apoptosis and the control of cell number
Cancer: oncogenes, tumour suppressors (p53, RB) and the multi-hit model
Cancer in Ghana and Africa: cervical, breast and liver cancer, screening and vaccination

units.title: Gene expression and its regulation
topics: The central dogma; DNA structure, replication and repair
Transcription in bacteria and the lac operon as a switch
Eukaryotic transcription: promoters, enhancers, transcription factors and chromatin
RNA processing: capping, splicing, polyadenylation and alternative splicing
Translation: the genetic code, ribosomes, tRNA and mutations
Epigenetics: DNA methylation and histone modification
Gene regulatory networks: Boolean and differential-equation models of switches and oscillators

units.title: Laboratory techniques and the data they produce
topics: Spectrophotometry and the Beer-Lambert law; standard curves
PCR and quantitative PCR: amplification curves, Ct values and relative expression
Gel electrophoresis and Western blotting: reading bands and sizing fragments
Sequencing, microarrays and mass spectrometry: what each assay measures and its noise
Experimental design: controls, replicates, batch effects and reproducibility

schedule.title: Chemistry of life and energy
schedule.exercise: Calculate the pH of a phosphate buffer from the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation, then use delta-G values to decide whether ATP hydrolysis can drive a given reaction.

tasks.title: Plot pH against added base for a weak acid with the maths lab, mark the pKa and buffering region, and read off the pH after adding 5 mmol base
Compute delta-G from standard free energy and concentrations for a reaction at 37 C, and plot how the sign of delta-G changes with product concentration
Step through two coupled reactions where ATP hydrolysis drives an unfavourable step, and compute the combined delta-G and equilibrium shift

schedule.title: Amino acids and the peptide backbone
schedule.exercise: Draw a tripeptide at pH 7, compute its net charge and isoelectric point, and classify each residue as polar, non-polar, acidic or basic.

tasks.title: Compute net charge across pH 1 to 13 for a given peptide from side-chain pKa values and find its isoelectric point from the plot
Plot phi and psi angles for 30 residues of a given structure on a Ramachandran plot and flag residues in disallowed regions
Walk through a protein fold in the visualiser, labelling primary to quaternary structure, and count helices, strands and hydrogen bonds for a given domain

schedule.title: Folding, haemoglobin and protein data
schedule.exercise: Explain why a single glutamate-to-valine change causes sickle cell disease, and describe the information stored in a PDB file header and ATOM records.

tasks.title: Parse a given PDB file with a short script, count residues per chain, and report the centre of mass and secondary-structure content
Fit the Hill equation to oxygen saturation data for haemoglobin and myoglobin and compare the Hill coefficients and P50 values
Work through a clinical case of a child with suspected sickle cell disease: choose tests, interpret electrophoresis evidence and counsel the family on inheritance

schedule.title: Enzyme catalysis and Michaelis-Menten
schedule.exercise: Derive the Michaelis-Menten equation from the steady-state assumption and use a Lineweaver-Burk plot and a non-linear fit to estimate Km and Vmax from the same data.

tasks.title: Plot reaction velocity against substrate for given Km and Vmax values, and read the velocity at Km, at 10 Km and at 0.1 Km
Fit Michaelis-Menten parameters to 12 noisy rate measurements by Lineweaver-Burk and by non-linear least squares, and compare both estimates with the true values
Write a script that fits Km and Vmax by non-linear least squares with bootstrap confidence intervals, and show how noise inflates linearised-plot error

schedule.title: Inhibition, allostery and assays
schedule.exercise: Identify the type of inhibition from a pair of double-reciprocal plots, and explain why an enzyme assay must measure initial rates only.

tasks.title: Overlay Lineweaver-Burk lines with and without inhibitor, classify the inhibition type from how the intercepts move, and report Ki
Extract initial rates from five progress curves where substrate depletes, and show the error from using a late time point instead
Simulate an allosteric enzyme with feedback inhibition by its end product, and plot how the pathway output responds to a step change in substrate

schedule.title: Metabolism overview and glycolysis
schedule.exercise: Write the net equation of glycolysis, list where ATP is spent and made, and say which step phosphofructokinase controls and why.

tasks.title: Step through the ten reactions of glycolysis, recording the ATP and NADH balance after each step and the net yield per glucose
Simulate glycolysis as ordinary differential equations with phosphofructokinase feedback, and plot metabolite levels as glucose supply doubles
Trace the carbons of labelled glucose through pyruvate oxidation and one turn of the citric acid cycle, and tabulate where each carbon ends up

schedule.title: Oxidative phosphorylation and metabolic control
schedule.exercise: Calculate the ATP yield per glucose with realistic P/O ratios, and explain how insulin and glucagon switch liver metabolism between storage and release.

tasks.title: Compute the proton-motive force from a pH difference and membrane potential, and estimate ATP produced per NADH and FADH2
Manage a case of a diabetic patient at a rural clinic: read glucose readings, decide insulin timing around meals, and justify the choices against the rubric
Write the stoichiometric matrix for a five-reaction pathway, solve for steady-state fluxes, and check mass balance for each metabolite

schedule.title: Membranes, transport and signalling
schedule.exercise: Compute the equilibrium potential of potassium and sodium from their concentrations, and trace a signal from a hormone binding a G-protein-coupled receptor to a cell response.

tasks.title: Calculate Nernst potentials for K, Na and Cl from given concentrations, then use the Goldman equation to predict resting membrane potential
Simulate the sodium-potassium pump and a leak channel in a cell model and watch concentrations and membrane voltage reach steady state
Model a two-step kinase cascade with feedback as differential equations, and plot response against dose to show amplification and saturation

schedule.title: Cells, organelles and the cell cycle
schedule.exercise: Draw the cell cycle with its checkpoints, say which cyclin-CDK pair drives each transition, and count chromosomes and DNA content at each stage of mitosis and meiosis.

tasks.title: Step through the cell cycle in the visualiser, marking checkpoints, and report what happens if the G1/S checkpoint fails to arrest a damaged cell
Compute the number of distinct gametes and the chance of a given chromosome combination in meiosis for an organism with n pairs of chromosomes
Fit a growth model to cell counts from a dividing culture and estimate the doubling time and fraction of cells in each phase

schedule.title: Apoptosis and cancer
schedule.exercise: Explain how loss of p53 lets damaged cells survive, and write a short brief on the case for HPV vaccination and cervical screening in Ghana.

tasks.title: Trace p53 response to DNA damage in a pathway diagram and predict the outcome of mutations in p53, MDM2 or RB
Fit a multi-hit model to age-incidence data for a cancer and estimate the number of rate-limiting mutations from the log-log slope
Run a screening-programme scenario for cervical cancer in a district: allocate limited tests, interpret results and balance coverage against follow-up capacity

schedule.title: DNA, transcription and regulation in bacteria
schedule.exercise: Describe the steps from a DNA sequence to a mature mRNA, and explain how the lac operon senses glucose and lactose.

tasks.title: Write a function to transcribe a DNA sequence to mRNA and find the reverse complement, and test it on three given genes
Model the lac operon as a switch using equations for repressor, inducer and enzyme levels, and plot the response across lactose concentrations
Implement splicing of a pre-mRNA from given exon boundaries, then enumerate the isoforms from skipping each internal exon

schedule.title: Translation, epigenetics and regulatory networks
schedule.exercise: Translate a short mRNA using the codon table, classify the effect of three point mutations, and sketch a Boolean network for a two-gene toggle switch.

tasks.title: Translate a given mRNA in all three reading frames, find the open reading frame, and classify each of five mutations as silent, missense or nonsense
Run a Boolean network of five genes from every initial state, and list the attractors and the states that lead to each
Simulate a repressilator of three genes as differential equations, vary the Hill coefficient, and find the parameter range that sustains oscillations

schedule.title: Laboratory techniques, data and project
schedule.exercise: Plan an experiment to compare gene expression in treated and untreated cells, listing controls, replicates and the assay data you will analyse; then present the lab data project.

tasks.title: Build a standard curve from absorbance readings using the Beer-Lambert law and calculate the concentration of three unknown samples with their error
Analyse a qPCR plate: find Ct values, normalise to a reference gene and compute fold change with the delta-delta Ct method
Review a flawed experiment in a case file: find missing controls, a batch effect and pseudoreplication, and rewrite the design to fix each
